message:
Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Solar Energy Systems Engineer, Enclosure and Structural Designer, Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, coverage is not yet even across functions. In plain words only regulation has two working controls while storage and cooling have only one owner with a working principle. Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer still owes a concept for Convert sunlight, Store energy, Enclose chamber and Hold produce, and Store energy and Remove heat still lack a second substantive principle from any member, with Enclosure and Structural Designer and Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist having posted no-principle statements for those functions. The two weakest functions are Store energy and Remove heat, for which Solar Energy Systems Engineer and Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer will each bring one distant analogy with a written mapping in cycle 2, and Enclosure and Structural Designer and Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist will add interface concepts for penetrations, drains and door discipline.

In plain words the box fits the tonne and the leak fits the cooling budget but the sun numbers do not yet agree and the sunshade does not fit the panels. Produce is 1000 kg from the total produce mass estimate (E49), about fourteen person weights in fifty shopping bags, inside 8.64 cubic metres from the interior volume estimate (E39), about a small bedroom a person can stand in at 2.0 m high, with conduction 203 W from the conduction estimate (E41) inside the 350 W steady assumption in the revised steady-load simulation (E28). The full-tonne pull-down is 25.0 kilowatt-hour from the recomputed pull-down estimate (E26), about two households daily use, so the 972 from the estimate produce sensible heat estimate (E12) is a unit error and is set aside, staged as 6.20 kilowatt-hour per 250 kg batch in that same revised steady-load simulation (E28). Array sizing at 2.13 kilowatt from the array sizing estimate (E13) yielding 9.00 kilowatt-hour per day from the daily yield estimate (E14) cannot cover 13.3 kilowatt-hour per day load with 5.41 kilowatt-hour left in the night autonomy simulation (E15) nor 15.3 kilowatt-hour per day in the steady heat load simulation (E27), about one to two households daily use, and nobody computed the critical array footprint of about 12 square metres for six 400 watt modules against a roof of about 4.3 square metres nor the summed ground mass of produce plus crates plus battery plus panels.

In plain words there is no blocking objection to resolve and all not-ready votes are sustained pending named evidence. There are no open blocking objections on the board. Solar Energy Systems Engineer, array size stays open until Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer locks steady and pull-down watts. Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer and Enclosure and Structural Designer, 350 watt steady and curtain choice stay open until door openings per day are locked by Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist and the 43 degree Celsius pull-down bench test is named by Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer. Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, single 5.0 degree Celsius setpoint and attendant role stay open for your confirmation in cycle 2.

RECORD: No concept is selected, numbers that stand are 1000 kg produce (E49) in 8.64 cubic metres (E39) with 25.4 square metres envelope (E40), conduction 203 W (E41) within 615 W average with staged pull-down and 6.20 kilowatt-hour per 250 kg batch (E28), pull-down 25.0 kilowatt-hour (E26) superseding (E12), Photovoltaic (PV, solar electricity) yield 9.00 kilowatt-hour per day at 2.40 kilowatt peak (E14) against loads 13.3 kilowatt-hour per day (E15) to 15.3 kilowatt-hour per day (E27) unresolved, still open are Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer concepts for four functions plus second principles for Store energy and Remove heat with distant analogies from Solar Energy Systems Engineer and Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, array footprint versus shade frame and summed mass and daily electric balance, setpoint and door discipline from Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, and bench test for 43 degree pull-down from Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer.

My position is not ready, because loads, array size and box interfaces are not yet reconciled to a buildable whole.
Note on Solar Energy Systems Engineer: strong sizing chain but daily loads inconsistent and footprint unchecked.
Note on Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer: corrected heat quantity and staged logic with clear service choice.
Note on Enclosure and Structural Designer: box volume and leak fit budget with clear ground and shade separation.
Note on Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist: crate count and handling limit anchor the tonne to daily work.
